graph_meta.problem_text: Last year, we hired 3 buses for the school trip. We had a total of 162 students and teachers who went on that trip and all the buses were full. This year we have 204 students and teachers. How many buses will we need? Will all the buses be full?
graph_meta.description: Solution DAG for finding per-bus capacity, then computing the number of buses needed and whether the final bus will be full.

nodes.label: Identify the Goal
nodes.description: Identify the quantity or decision the problem asks for.
nodes.prompt: What do we need to find?
accept: how many buses are needed and whether they will be full
hints: State clearly what the question asks you to determine.

nodes.label: Identify Given Information
nodes.description: Identify the facts and quantities provided in this word problem.
nodes.prompt: What information is given in the problem?
accept: 3 full buses carry 162 people and this year there are 204 people
hints: Read the problem carefully and identify the quantities and relationships.

nodes.label: Problem Statement
nodes.description: Each bus was full last year, so one bus carries 162 ÷ 3 students and teachers.
nodes.prompt: Find the capacity of one bus, then decide how many buses are needed for 204 people.

nodes.label: Final Conclusion
nodes.description: Four buses are needed, and they will not all be full because 204 ÷ 54 ≈ 3.78 and 4 × 54 = 216.
nodes.prompt: State how many buses are needed and whether all of them will be full.
accept: 4 buses, not full because 12 seats are empty
hints: So they will not all be full.

nodes.label: Method 1: Find bus capacity
nodes.description: Divide 162 by 3 to find the number of students and teachers per bus.
nodes.prompt: Use the full capacity from last year's trip.
hints: The 4th bus will not be full.

nodes.label: Compute per-bus capacity
nodes.prompt: What is the capacity of one bus?

nodes.label: Find required buses
nodes.description: 204 ÷ 54 ≈ 3.78, so 4 buses are needed. 4 × 54 = 216 seats, so not all buses are full.
nodes.prompt: How many buses are needed for 204 people? Will all the buses be full?
hints: 4 × 54 = 216, so the last bus is not full.
